correctness.rationale: PASS: The four one-digit contributions 0,1,6,7 have distinct residues mod4; comparing least differing base-four digit proves injectivity of (x,y)→x+6y for all finite M digit strings. The complete three-state carry map ((0,0,1,1),(2,0,0,1),(2,2,0,0)) follows from per-digit equation ε+6η+c=d+4c_next. Exactly two transitions to final carry0 from each state yields a_L=2·4^{L-1}; b_{L+1}=2a_L+b_L and b_1=2 yields b_L=(4^L+2)/3. Counting leading digit0/1 yields F(2·4^L)=2a_L+b_L. The subsequential normalized counts tend to distinct 1/2 and 2/3; no claim that these are global liminf/sup. Independent explicit sums n<3000 confirmed uniqueness, carry acceptance and both formulas for L=1..5; source verifier extends finite checks to 131072. Infinite proof rests on exact automaton recurrences.

value.rationale: PASS: M+2M is the canonical perfect-coverage digital basis. c=6 is the first coefficient greater than two preserving local injectivity of all four digit-pair residues; its explicit failure of natural density is a meaningful qualitative boundary. The two infinite exact counting sequences show how a natural sparse additive sumset can oscillate between 1/2 and 2/3 cutoff proportions despite unique representations. This is neither a random finite cutoff nor known-table recomputation.
